subject: Request: Narrow p95 observation window for high-throughput tenants (Luminex)
messages:
From: Max Rivera <max@luminexhealth.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: Karen Diaz <karen.diaz@luminexhealth.com>, procurement@luminexhealth.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: p95 spikes — request to adjust measurement window for Luminex tenant

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’ve been validating the hosted API in our pre-prod environment and noticed recurring short-duration latency spikes that push our observed p95 over the committed threshold. The pattern: a 3–6 minute tail once per day coinciding with our nightly batch ingestion (ETL) that fans out a large number of short requests.

Attached is our dashboard extract showing the daily spikes and a short note with what we believe is the root cause. Because the spike is short but regular, the current p95 measurement window amplifies it in ways that impact our alerting and contract calculations.

We’d like to request a formal exception or an adjustment to how p95 is measured for our tenant during the onboarding period: specifically, either (A) exclude automated bulk-ingestion windows from p95 calculation via a mutually-agreed maintenance window, or (B) adopt a rolling 1-hour p95 aggregation for billing/credit purposes (instead of the current 5-minute window).

Our ask: can Redwood propose which option would be operationally simplest, outline the control-plane changes (if any), and confirm any implications for credits, monitoring, and SLO dashboards? We’re targeting a 3-month pilot for this adjustment while we rework the ETL to smooth the fan-out.

I’ve cc’d Karen and procurement so we can keep contract/finance in the loop. I can jump on a short call this week to walk the dashboard.

Thanks,
Max Rivera
Director of Infrastructure
Luminex Health

Attachment: Luminex_SLO_p95_exception_request.pdf (summary + dashboard)

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Max Rivera <max@luminexhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: p95 spikes — request to adjust measurement window for Luminex tenant

Max — thanks for the detail and the dashboard extract. I reviewed the attachment and forwarded the graf to Rishi and Marissa for SRE and contract impact review. High level response: we can support a temporary exception while you stabilize ETL, but we need to land on an exact measurement and operational guardrails so the exception doesn’t create regressions for other tenants.

Proposed next steps from my side:
- Rishi to triage technical feasibility (control-plane, observability) and recommend whether a maintenance window exclusion or a different aggregation window is cleaner.
- Marissa to draft contract language for a 90-day exception and describe credit mechanics if SLO is breached outside the exception.
- Schedule a 30-min sync on Wednesday (I’m available 10–11am PT) to align on telemetry and timelines.

Can you confirm the daily ETL window (local time) and whether you can tolerate a scheduled maintenance exclusion for that 10–15 minute period? If you can, that is usually the fastest path.

I’ll attach a short checklist we use for these pilots.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

Attachment: luminex-monthly-p95-dashboard.csv (sample)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, Max Rivera <max@luminexhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: p95 spikes — request to adjust measurement window for Luminex tenant

On Tue, Jun 29, 2026 at 08:45 AM ava_chen@redwood.com wrote:
> Max — thanks for the detail and the dashboard extract. I reviewed the attachment and forwarded the graf to Rishi and Marissa for SRE and contract impact review.

Max / Ava — quick technical note from SRE: we can implement a tenant-level exception that either (1) marks a 10–20 minute maintenance window as excluded from billing/SLO computation, or (2) changes the aggregation period used for p95 from a 5-minute rolling bucket to a 1-hour rolling bucket for the Luminex tenant’s billing view.

Tradeoffs:
- Excluded maintenance window: minimal runtime changes, explicit control, preserves global SLO stats. Requires the tenant to request/confirm schedule and will not help if spikes shift outside that window.
- 1-hour rolling p95: more forgiving to short spikes but requires changes to how we compute and display p95 in our billing pipeline and may impact alerting thresholds. Implementation estimated 3–5 business days of dev effort + QA.

Recommendation: Implement the exclusion window for an immediate relief pilot (no code path changes) and run the 1-hour rolling p95 in parallel as a billing calculation experiment for 90 days. If the 1-hour aggregate proves stable, we can make it part of a formal amendment.

Operational asks for Luminex:
1) Confirm the ETL start time and the typical duration.
2) Approve a recurring daily exclusion window of 10 minutes for the pilot (we’ll log it and exclude from SLO math).
3) Accept that any credits/true-ups will be determined after the 90-day evaluation using the agreed calculation.

I can spin up an internal runbook and a one-off billing job for the 1-hour experiment once we have sign-off.

— Rishi Malhotra
VP, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Max Rivera <max@luminexhealth.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Karen Diaz <karen.diaz@luminexhealth.com>, procurement@luminexhealth.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: p95 spikes — request to adjust measurement window for Luminex tenant

Thanks all — good alignment. Max / Karen: can you confirm the ETL daily window below so we can schedule the exclusion pilot?

Luminex proposed ETL window (from dashboard): 02:10–02:20 PT daily (approx 7–12 minutes).
Redwood pilot plan (proposed):
- Phase 1 (immediate): Add a recurring daily SLO exclusion window 02:05–02:25 PT (20 minutes) for Luminex for 90 days. This will be excluded from billing SLO math and alerts. No changes required to runtime.
- Phase 2 (parallel experiment): Run a billing calculation that computes 1-hour rolling p95 for the same period to compare impact (retrospective, non-billing). Estimated dev effort: 3–5 business days.
- Phase 3 (decision): After 90 days, review metrics and agree on whether to convert the 1-hour aggregation into the contract or revert to standard measurements. Credits (if any) to be negotiated based on delta outside exclusion windows.

Please reply with one of the following: "CONFIRM ETL WINDOW" or "REQUEST ALTERNATIVE WINDOW" and whether procurement should draft the 90-day addendum now. I’ll ask Marissa to prepare draft language and Rishi to schedule the billing experiment.

Thanks — ava
